records.trigger_condition: Customer Tracker Sync or any Stripe-dependent workflow runs while the Stripe account is in TEST mode / pre-KYC (charges_enabled false)
records.name: Stripe Test-Data Contamination Guard
records.remediation_steps:
1. BEFORE any Stripe-to-Tracker sync write, verify the account is LIVE: GET /v1/account and check charges_enabled AND livemode
2. If charges_enabled is false (pre-KYC) or livemode is false: EXIT SILENTLY — do not poll subscriptions further, do not write ANY rows, even if data was already fetched (observed Sept 4: 12 test subscriptions polled then Graph write failed — the failed write was accidentally protective)
3. Never write test-mode Stripe customers/subscriptions to the real Customer_Tracker.xlsx or the hub Customer entity — that contaminates the real ledger
4. Log the skip to RateLimitLog with the reason so the silence is auditable
5. Once Leon provides the live key post-KYC, the sync activates automatically with real data only

records.trigger_condition: Workflow agent step fails to create PlatformAlert / TelemetryEvent / SystemHealth records due to entity validation errors (missing customer_id, metadata as string)
records.name: Workflow Entity-Validation Rejection Fix
records.remediation_steps:
1. When an entity write from a workflow is rejected by validation, capture the exact validation error
2. Known contracts: PlatformAlert and TelemetryEvent REQUIRE customer_id (use 'squirl-os-technologies' for hub ops); metadata fields must be JSON dictionary objects, never strings
3. Reshape the payload to the validation contract and retry once
4. If the entity schema itself is wrong, log the mismatch — do NOT improvise a different entity as a workaround (that creates orphan records; observed Sept 4 when an idempotency marker landed in RemediationSweep)
5. On success, verify the record landed in the INTENDED entity

records.trigger_condition: Cross-app bridge function (aegisAnomalySync / technicianTicketSync) returns timeout or MongoDB connection error
records.name: Cross-App Bridge Timeout Recovery
records.remediation_steps:
1. On aegisAnomalySync / technicianTicketSync timeout (MongoDB 20s) DO NOT conclude the bridge is unavailable — timeouts are usually transient
2. Retry the SAME call once (observed: first call timed out, retry succeeded in 6s, Sept 4, 2026)
3. If second call fails, split the payload into smaller batches (2-3 records per call)
4. If still failing, log the failure with the exact error string and defer to the next reconciliation window (7am/7pm CT) — never leave partial state silently; report which records did and did not sync
5. Never fall back to destructive operations; the bridge functions are the only sanctioned cross-app write path

records.trigger_condition: QB-Sentinel customer count differs from stored baseline (413) without a Master Demo run in the window, OR count decreases
records.name: QBO Demo-Customer Drift Reconciliation
records.remediation_steps:
1. Pull QBO customers ORDERBY MetaData.CreateTime DESC (limit 15)
2. Compare count vs baseline (413 as of Sept 4, 2026)
3. Classify each new record: sim/demo artifact (created during demo window, demo-style names like 'Master Demo Corp *') vs REAL customer
4. Demo artifacts = HEALTHY growth — report count, update baseline, NO action (sim data is permanent, never deleted)
5. Real drift (count DECREASED or unexplained growth): record-level reconciliation against hub Customer entity only — NEVER bulk-sync, NEVER delete, NEVER deactivate without Leon's approval
6. Log heartbeat + healing event with the classification result

records.trigger_condition: iPhone gaming: stutter/heat during play, 60fps games on 120Hz devices, or storage pressure — GUIDED MODE ONLY (Apple sandbox)
records.name: iOS Gaming Conditions (guided, honest scope)
records.remediation_steps:
1. HONEST SCOPE: Apple controls the scheduler — we optimize CONDITIONS, not performance directly
2. Low Power Mode check: it caps refresh rate + CPU — OFF during play (guided toggle)
3. 120Hz-capable device: verify refresh not limited by settings
4. Thermal conditions: avoid charging while playing graphically heavy titles (heat = throttle) + case-off advisory — guided
5. Background App Refresh off for non-essential apps (guided walkthrough)
6. Storage >10% free (offload unused apps) — games thrash when storage is full
7. Reduce Motion for older devices (user choice, parallax cost)
8. Health report card + session log to hub — no FPS magic claims, conditions only

records.trigger_condition: Linux gaming rig or Steam Deck: Proton game stutters, low FPS vs Windows parity, or missing GameMode/HUD tooling
records.name: Linux Gaming (Steam Proton + Steam Deck)
records.remediation_steps:
1. GameMode check (Feral gamemoderun): installed + wired into game launch commands
2. MangoHud optional: on-screen perf overlay (GPU/CPU/temps/frametime) — recommendation, user choice
3. vm.max_map_count check (some modern titles need higher; default 65530) — sysctl set with user approval, documented in /etc/sysctl.d
4. Vulkan/Mesa driver version check (vulkaninfo) — old Mesa = stutters; recommend distro-appropriate update path
5. Proton version per game: verify Steam per-game Proton override matches known-good; Proton-GE guidance only (never auto-install)
6. Compositor: report fullscreen unredirect state (GNOME auto; KDE configurable)
7. Steam Deck: official paths ONLY — no unsupported kernel hacks (Decky plugins explicitly out of scope)
8. Measure frametimes before/after — log real deltas

records.trigger_condition: Linux machine: /var or /home filling, apt cache bloat, or free disk space below 15%
records.name: Linux Disk Recovery (journal, apt, flatpak, caches)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Measure: journalctl --disk-usage, du on ~/.cache, /var/cache, old kernels, flatpak/snap sprawl
2. journald vacuum to 7 days (systemctl restart systemd-journald after)
3. apt clean + autoremove --purge (KEEP current kernel + one previous — human approval for any kernel removal)
4. flatpak uninstall --unused; snap removal only for disabled snaps (report first)
5. Browser/thumbnail caches cleared
6. SSD detected (rotational=0): fstrim -av — NEVER defrag SSDs
7. Report MB reclaimed per category + free-space delta

records.trigger_condition: Linux local machine (Ubuntu/Debian/Arch incl. Steam Deck): systemd failed units, service crash loops, or degraded system state
records.name: Linux Failed Service Repair (systemd)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Scan: systemctl --failed — list failed units
2. Per unit: journalctl -u <unit> --since -24h for root cause before any restart
3. Restart failed unit (systemctl restart), verify active state
4. reset-failed after verified stable 60s
5. Dependency audit: units failed because a target failed vs unit-level crash — fix the parent, not the symptom
6. Log AegisHealingEvent to local queue (syncs when online)
7. Never mask/disable units without human approval — masking a failed unit hides the problem

records.trigger_condition: Gamer reports lag/rubber-banding while system performance is healthy, or jitter/packet loss detected on baseline
records.name: Gaming Network Tuning (latency + bufferbloat)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Latency/jitter/packet-loss baseline to common game service endpoints (multi-ping)
2. Wi-Fi vs Ethernet detection: Wi-Fi with evidence of jitter = recommend Ethernet cable with the numbers shown
3. DNS latency comparison (current vs alternatives) — switch only with user approval
4. Bufferbloat quick test (loaded latency vs idle) — router QoS guidance is a HUMAN task, we provide the report card
5. Router reboot recommendation if uptime months-long (ISP gateway instability)
6. NO registry snake-oil tweaks — documented, reversible, evidence-based only

records.trigger_condition: Gaming machine: FPS drops as sessions lengthen, stutters under load, or sustained clocks below base frequency
records.name: Thermal Throttle Detection (evidence, not magic)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Load test: CPU clock under load vs rated base clock (Win32_PerfFormattedData) — sustained clock < base = throttling
2. Thermal zone temps via WMI where sensors exposed
3. Frame-time correlation: stutter timing vs clock dips — evidence report the user can see
4. Dust/debris advisory (we can't blow dust out remotely — honest guidance + cleaning guide)
5. Laptop power slider check: performance mode engaged while gaming
6. Fan curve: report vendor-tool state, never override safety curves
7. Case airflow + ambient temp questionnaire — simple, high-signal

records.trigger_condition: Gaming machine: stutters after hours of play, RAM pressure during gaming, or multiple RGB/launcher suites detected
records.name: Gaming RAM Recovery (standby leak + background bloat)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Detect standby memory leak pattern: standby list huge + free RAM low after long session (Get-Counter memory counters)
2. Honest fix first: scheduled reboot recommendation (safe, effective) — no sketchy kernel-level list-purge tools
3. Background bloat audit WHILE a game is running: top RAM consumers (RGB suites, launchers, updaters running simultaneously)
4. Tie into PB-WIN-STARTUP-TRIM-001 — the real fix is bloat not returning at boot
5. RGB/launcher ecosystem report: 3+ sync suites (iCUE + Synapse + Armoury Crate together) is a known RAM/CPU tax — recommend consolidation, user choice
6. Log RAM before/after

records.trigger_condition: Gaming machine: driver crashes (Event ID 14/nvlddmkm patterns), GPU vendor swap leftovers, or driver age > 12 months with symptoms
records.name: GPU Driver Hygiene (clean install path)
records.remediation_steps:
1. GPU detection (Win32_VideoController): model, driver version, date
2. Flag: driver older than 12 months, known-bad versions in KB, or vendor mismatch (NVIDIA driver remnants after AMD swap and vice versa)
3. Leftover detection: orphaned driver packages (pnputil enum), old vendor folders
4. Clean install path is DDU-guided in safe mode — HUMAN-GATED, we guide step-by-step, never auto-execute
5. Rollback preserved: always record previous driver version in healing log
6. Post-install verify: driver active, HAGS state re-checked

records.trigger_condition: Steam: long load times, corrupt game files, failed updates, or games installed on HDD with SSD available
records.name: Steam Game File + Library Repair
records.remediation_steps:
1. Library drive type detection (SSD vs HDD) — games on HDD: report load-time evidence + recommend SSD migration (user decision)
2. HDD libraries ONLY: defragment game files (Steam defrag logic) — NEVER defrag SSDs
3. Verify integrity of game files (Steam console command) — repair corrupt files automatically (safe, checksum-driven)
4. Library free space check — Steam updates fail silently when full
5. Archive/move redundant depotcache + old download chunks
6. Log per-library health report

records.trigger_condition: Steam client: slow downloads, shader-stutter in games, overlay conflicts, or client instability
records.name: Steam Client Health (download region, shader cache, overlays)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Download region check vs user location — wrong region = slow downloads + patching pain
2. Shader cache size/corruption check — clear ONLY when corrupted (corrupt cache = stutters in cached games), never routine
3. Overlay audit: Steam + Discord + GeForce/NVIDIA + Xbox overlays running together cause conflicts — flag multiples, recommend keeping ONE
4. Steam client service health check
5. Download throttle settings audit
6. Log findings + user-approved changes only

records.trigger_condition: Windows gaming machine: FPS lower than hardware-class expectation, stutter in fullscreen titles, or background recording detected active
records.name: Game Mode + Game DVR Audit (the classic FPS thief)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Verify Windows Game Mode ENABLED (gaming settings)
2. Detect Game DVR / Xbox background recording state (GameDVR_Enabled registry + policy) — background recording steals 5-15% FPS in many titles
3. If on: present evidence + user approval, then disable background recording (never touches user's clips already saved)
4. Report Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling (HAGS) state — toggle ONLY with user approval (driver-dependent)
5. Per-game fullscreen optimizations: report current state, user's choice
6. Before/after measurement plan: user runs game's built-in benchmark, we log real deltas — no invented numbers

records.trigger_condition: iOS device NOT enrolled in MDM (personal/BYOD): user reports slowdown, storage full, or mail bloat — GUIDED ONLY, no autonomous repair possible on iOS
records.name: iOS Personal Device Guided Cleanup (non-MDM)
records.remediation_steps:
1. HONEST SCOPE: Apple sandboxing forbids local daemons repairing system services — no autonomous agent on-device
2. Run guided Shortcuts pack with user: storage review, Offload Unused Apps, on-device mail cleanup rules, Safari clear history walkthrough
3. Deliver health report card to user (battery, storage, update status)
4. Recommend Apple Business Manager enrollment for full MDM control (the honest upsell)
5. Log guidance session to hub — machine remains user-controlled
6. Flag device as 'unmanaged — guided mode' in asset inventory

records.trigger_condition: iOS device ENROLLED in Intune/Jamf (via Apple Business Manager): degraded performance, storage pressure, stale OS, or app policy violation
records.name: iOS Repair via MDM Plane (Intune/Jamf)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Pull device telemetry: storage breakdown, battery health, OS version, app inventory
2. Remote restart via MDM (graceful)
3. Push pending OS updates (supervised devices)
4. Remove flagged apps per policy (supervised only, policy-driven)
5. Storage guidance: Offload Unused Apps recommendation + report
6. Safari/browser data cannot be remotely cleared on iOS — Apple restriction, documented honestly
7. Verify device checks in + log to hub

records.trigger_condition: Local machine: Defender detection, suspicious process behavior, or ransomware indicators (all machines — highest escalation priority)
records.name: Malware First Response (local)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Defender quick scan (full scan only if quick scan flags something)
2. Quarantine findings automatically (within Defender's own authority)
3. Collect: process list, startup anomalies, scheduled task anomalies, unusual network connections
4. NEVER remove beyond Defender quarantine without human approval — always escalated
5. Isolation recommendation to user (disconnect network if critical)
6. Critical severity: PredictiveAlert + human acknowledgment gate before any further action
7. Log full forensic snapshot (no PII in logs per policy)

records.trigger_condition: Any machine: mailbox bloat, suspicious rules detected, BEC indicators, or user reports email chaos
records.name: Cloud Mailbox Hygiene (Graph, any machine)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Audit inbox rules — flag any forwarding/redirect to external addresses (BEC defense)
2. Present suspicious rules to user — NEVER auto-delete a rule without human approval
3. Sweep quarantine + junk with report
4. Subscription-bloat digest: recurring sender list + one-click unsubscribe suggestions
5. Archive mail older than 12 months to online archive (user approval, batched)
6. Works identically on domain and non-domain machines — the mailbox lives in the cloud
7. Log hygiene metrics to hub (no message content — privacy rule)

records.trigger_condition: DOMAIN-JOINED only: machine can't reach DC, intermittent auth prompts, or domain resource access failures
records.name: Domain Client Service Stack (local)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Verify Netlogon, Workstation, DNS Client services running + set Automatic
2. Test DNS resolution of domain + DC FQDNs
3. Check cached credential count (report only, no registry change)
4. Verify firewall Domain profile allows domain traffic
5. Restart failed services per PB-WIN-SVC-RESTART-001 protocol
6. Verify domain logon succeeds end-to-end

records.trigger_condition: DOMAIN-JOINED only: trust relationship failures, Kerberos errors, GPO not applying, slow domain logons
records.name: Domain-Joined Machine Health (trust + auth)
records.remediation_steps:
1. nltest /sc_query — verify secure channel to DC
2. Test-ComputerSecureChannel — if false: credential-free repair first, then with hub-held service account (human-gated)
3. klist purge — clear stale Kerberos tickets
4. Verify DC DNS SRV records resolve (_ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs)
5. w32tm /query — verify time sync (Kerberos 5-min skew rule)
6. gpupdate /force — re-apply policy
7. Re-test domain auth + log result

records.trigger_condition: Local machine: recurring error patterns (Event ID clustering) or degraded performance with no obvious cause
records.name: Windows Event Log Triage (local)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Scan System + Application logs: critical/error events last 72h
2. Group by source + event ID, rank by frequency
3. Match signature against known playbook triggers (service crash, disk, update, network patterns)
4. Auto-remediate matched low-risk patterns; flag unknowns for review
5. Emit anomaly records to local queue for hub sync + pattern learning
6. Never clear logs — evidence is preserved

records.trigger_condition: Local machine: slow boot (>60s) or high idle CPU/RAM from background bloat
records.name: Startup and Background App Trim (local)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Inventory: startup folder, Run/RunOnce keys, scheduled tasks, Automatic services with no business need
2. Categorize: required / recommended / bloat (never touch security agents or the SQUIRL runtime)
3. Present trim list to user — human approval gate before disable
4. Disable approved items (startup registry + task scheduler disable)
5. Measure boot time before/after
6. Log delta + keep rollback list to re-enable in one command

records.trigger_condition: Local machine: Outlook hangs, not syncing, stuck outbox, or OST corruption (domain and non-domain)
records.name: Outlook Local Client Repair (local)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Triage: OST file size, sync state, outbox items stuck, error dialogs
2. Outlook safe-mode boot test (isolates add-in faults)
3. Disable flagged add-ins (report which — user approval to keep any)
4. Rebuild OST (delete + let resync from cloud — mailbox is source of truth, never at risk)
5. Flush stuck outbox items
6. Profile repair: new profile with same account if OST rebuild fails
7. Verify send/receive + log healing event

records.trigger_condition: Local machine: Windows Update stuck, failing repeatedly, or update service errors
records.name: Windows Update Repair (local)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Detect: pending updates stuck > 24h, error codes 0x8024xxxx
2. Stop wuauserv + bits + cryptsvc
3. Clear SoftwareDistribution\Download + catroot2 rename sequence (standard procedure)
4. Restart services, force detection (UsoClient StartScan)
5. If still failing: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth then sfc /scannow
6. Human gate before any feature-update install
7. Verify update progresses + log exit code

records.trigger_condition: Local machine: 'no internet' or intermittent connectivity on an otherwise healthy network
records.name: Network Stack Repair (local)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Triage: adapter state, IP config, gateway ping, DNS resolution test
2. ipconfig /flushdns
3. Winsock reset (netsh winsock reset) if resolution failing
4. NIC power-management check (disable allow-computer-to-turn-off)
5. Driver date/health check — flag outdated drivers, never auto-install
6. Re-test connectivity + latency, log result

records.trigger_condition: Local machine: free disk space below 15% or storage-related performance degradation
records.name: Windows Disk Space Recovery (local)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Scan: temp files, Windows Update cache (SoftwareDistribution), Delivery Optimization, recycle bin, minidumps
2. Report findings to user before deletion (human approval gate)
3. Clean approved categories via cleanmgr-equivalent PowerShell
4. Optional: hibernation file resize (user approval)
5. Generate large-file report (top 20) — never auto-delete user files
6. Verify free space delta

records.trigger_condition: Local machine: browser slow, cache > 500MB, or disk pressure traced to browser data
records.name: Browser Cache and Junk Cleanup (local)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Close browsers gracefully (warn user first)
2. Clear Chrome/Edge/Firefox cache dirs (%LocalAppData% paths) — never passwords/bookmarks/extensions
3. Clear temp + %TEMP% + Crashpad leftovers
4. Optional user-approved: cookie clear (prompted, default skip)
5. Relaunch browser + verify profile intact
6. Report MB reclaimed + startup time delta

records.trigger_condition: Local machine: Windows service in stopped/stopping state unexpectedly, or repeatedly crashing (non-domain and domain-joined both)
records.name: Stuck Windows Service Restart (local)
records.remediation_steps:
1. Identify service: Get-Service status + last exit code
2. Graceful stop with 30s timeout
3. Kill orphaned PIDs holding the service (taskkill /F only if graceful fails)
4. Set service recovery actions: restart on failure x3
5. Restart service + verify Running state + start all dependents
6. Verify with 60s soak + event log check for repeat crash pattern
7. Log AegisHealingEvent to local queue (syncs to hub when online)
